_comment: CLDR's answer to 'which scripts are written right-to-left', checked in as a
fixture because CI has no network and an oracle you cannot consult is not an
oracle.
Source: cldr-json cldr-core/scriptMetadata.json, version 48.2.0 --
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/main/cldr-json/cldr-core/scriptMetadata.json
Every entry here is a script whose `rtl` field is exactly "YES".
WHY THIS FILE AND NOT `Intl.Locale#getTextInfo()`: that API answers about a
LOCALE's layout, not a script's direction. `sq-Todr-AL` reports `ltr` because
CLDR says ALBANIAN is laid out left-to-right -- it says nothing about Todhri.
An earlier round of the application contract used it as the oracle and reached the right verdict
on `Todr` for the wrong reason. Pinning a parity table to a proxy would encode
a subtly wrong contract into the one artifact whose job is stopping the two
tiers from drifting -- and both tiers being consistently wrong is worse than
one being wrong, because the table would then PROVE them equal.
It also only sees entries that are PRESENT. Against this file the merged set
had two discrepancies, not one: `Todr` (rtl=NO, remove) and `Sidt` (rtl=YES,
missing). A proxy that inspects existing entries could never have found the
second.
Updating this file is a deliberate act: refetch from the URL above, bump the
version, and expect the direction tests to tell you exactly what changed.
